items.title: ATP Finals tennis: Carlos Alcaraz v Ben Shelton – live semi-final updates
items.summary:
ATP Finals updates from the last four in Turin
Mail Katy | Men’s $350m prize money boost

So who wins today? Well, so much depends on Alcaraz’s physical condition. If his hamstring doesn’t hinder him, he should win, given the heights he’s hit this week and during the past two months. His shot-making was devastating against Cobolli yesterday, when he deliberately kept the points short and sharp to protect his injury. First-strike tennis is Shelton’s forte, though, so expect plenty of indoor fireworks between these two showmen and explosive hitters. And being a left-hander, Shelton will hope his ferocious cross-court forehand can stretch Alcaraz on the backhand side and put pressure on that injured hamstring. Shelton’s biggest weapon, of course though, is his serve.

As for the head-to-head, Alcaraz leads 4-1, with Shelton’s only victory coming in that US Open quarter-final in September. Alcaraz has beaten Shelton indoors twice before: in the Paris Masters final two weeks ago and at the Laver Cup in 2024.

items.summary:

Elon Musk’s lawyer is joining Tom Brady in buying a stake in Chelsea. The Guardian revealed on Friday that the NFL player is in discussions about purchasing a minority shareholding at Stamford Bridge and can now disclose that Alex Spiro of the New York law firm Quinn Emmanuel is also seeking to buy a stake by investing in Chelsea’s majority owners, Clearlake Capital.

Brady and Spiro, who is representing planned Fifa investor Joshua Kushner in a legal battle against Uefa, would become limited partners in Clearlake with no voting rights at Chelsea if the transactions are completed.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI appears to mock NFL sexual misconduct scandals in radio parody
items.summary:
• Comedian Stavros Halkias voices fictional shock jock

  • Segment echoes Watson, Tucker misconduct allegations

  • Rockstar’s latest skewers American sports culture

The long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI appears to have taken aim at the NFL’s sexual misconduct scandals – and the culture of excuses surrounding them – with a satirical segment on the video game’s fictional conservative talk radio station bearing striking similarities to allegations against Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson and Kansas City Chiefs kicker Justin Tucker.

The segment features comedian and voice actor Stavros Halkias defending Anthony Ross, a fictional player for the Vice City Manatees, after an “alleged” incident involving a team masseuse. Although neither Watson nor Tucker are mentioned by name, the circumstances closely resemble allegations made against both players.

items.title: Pochettino the connector: will human touch lift Manchester United?
items.summary:
Argentinian has excelled in man-management – but will need his powers to energise new squad and impress owners

Mauricio Pochettino celebrated his 50th birthday in style. It was March 2022, he was in charge at Paris Saint-Germain and the venue was a stunning boutique hotel; the kind that many capitals have but only Paris truly does. Pochettino’s family and friends were there. So were his inner coaching circle, who are basically family. There were lots of people from PSG. And a good time was had by all.

For Pochettino, it was emotional. As everybody knows, the new Manchester United head coach is the kind of guy to well up when the speeches start, so imagine how he felt when he looked up at the big screen and a video montage of well-wishers started to roll.

items.title: Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet
items.summary:
The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player

Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality.

He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor & Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session.

Continue reading...
items.t: Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet

items.title: Rotated Wales aim to turn New Zealand miracle into true momentum against Australia
items.summary:
Steve Tandy has made four changes to his team to face wounded Wallabies after heroics against All Blacks

They beat the All Blacks for the first time in 73 years and they make four changes. The Wales coaching team could barely have shrugged their shoulders with any more nonchalance after what the rest of us thought was a pretty spectacular achievement last weekend if they had picked their under-20s for Saturday night’s follow-up against Australia in Cardiff. But, no, they are actually adding depth as well as quality to this new generation tasked with keeping the creaking structures of Welsh rugby upright for the foreseeable.

If anything, the changes make the team stronger. No matter they are without Adam Beard (shoulder injury but hopefully back for the finals next weekend), they see fit to drop/rest/let-attend-birth-of-first-child three other players too, including the player of the match last weekend.

Continue reading...

items.title: Men’s tennis boosts prize money for players to more than $350m in major overhaul
items.summary:
• Cash increase via ATP’s creation of ‘One Vision’ company

  • More rest breaks added to reduce player welfare issues

The Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) has approved major changes to the financial structure of men’s tennis that will make the total prize money available to the players increase to more than $350m (£267m) by 2028, from $270m this year.

The creation of a new company to sell all the tour’s media, commercial and data rights, ATP Ventures, will lead to the investment of an additional $100m in player remuneration including an increased $50m bonus pool, a $25m year-end rankings bonus and $26m player pensions.

Continue reading...
items.t: Major changes in men’s tennis will take prize money for players to more than $350m

items.title: Lewis Hamilton is now the apex sports protester as US athletes stay silent
items.summary:
The Ferrari driver has always used his fame to highlight causes he cares about. Now he stands out as other athletes tone down their rhetoric

Most Formula One drivers might slip away to the beach or the golf course on a week off between races. Lewis Hamilton is not most drivers, though. Instead he went to the Rafah border crossing between Egypt and Gaza. He greeted aid workers in Arabic, toured the checkpoint and visited the Egyptian Red Crescent warehouses in nearby El-Arish, where relief supplies are prepared for distribution. Hamilton made the visit on a day Israeli airstrikes and gunfire killed at least seven Palestinians in Gaza, adding to a death toll that’s climbed above 74,000 since war broke out three years ago. He wore dark glasses and dressed head to toe in black.

“The past three years of Israel’s genocide in Gaza is appalling,” he wrote on Instagram of his visit, before turning the lens on himself. “I know so many people that feel that same helplessness. That same need to do something rather than watch. I don’t want us to get used to their suffering. I don’t want us to look away.”

Continue reading...
items.t: Lewis Hamilton is now the apex sports protester as US athletes stay silent
